label: Low-Poly Skit
tagline: Faceted toy people act out a fast story in small 3D dioramas, a new shot every second.

messages.mascot: Mascots are not available in the Low-Poly Skit style: its cast is one house figure built from basic 3D shapes, and a flat mascot picture would not sit in its world. Choose another visual style, or no mascot.
messages.inserts: A Low-Poly Skit video takes no insert scenes: it is one continuous 3D world cut every second or so, and an insert would break it apart. Set Inserts to None, or choose another visual style.

review:
- This video is a Low-Poly Skit, and the following are its intended, approved look: flat-shaded toy people about four heads tall with faceted heads, blank dot eyes and a mouth that never moves with the speech; small diorama sets (a room with its front wall off, a stage, a street, a planet, a cross-section) standing on a plain grey or dark void; flat colours with visible facets, NO outlines and NO cast shadows; hard cuts about every second; a slow push-in on most shots; a sharp camera jolt on every footstep and impact; a yellow star burst, flying white chips and a red comic word on a hit; crowds of hundreds of the same figure in different colours; a smeared frame during a quick whip move; white captions that turn yellow word by word. Do NOT report any of these as defects, and do not suggest outlines, shading, shadows, realistic faces or lip sync: their absence is the style. A figure that falls or snaps between two poses in two or three frames is intended.
- Do report: a figure or prop passing through a wall or floor so that part of it is hidden, a figure cut off by the frame edge or standing under the caption band, a picture that shows something different from what the narration says at that moment, the same shot held for more than about three seconds with nothing changing, a crowd that is a flat colour block with no variety, and text drawn in the world (a sign, a clock) that is unreadable or cut off.
script:
Every beat's `visual` is a **shot** brief: the one small set it is in (a bedroom, a stage, a street, the planet from space, a cutaway of the ground), who is in it and what they are doing, and the single thing that changes. A beat is about one second of narration, so a sentence is one shot or two.

The narration speaks to "you" and follows what happens next: a situation, then a consequence, then a bigger consequence. Write it as a chain, each sentence one new place or one new action, and let the scale climb (a room, a street, a city, the planet) until the last link is the answer or the twist. Keep sentences short, about six to ten words, so a new picture can start on most of them, and say the thing that is on screen by name ("the broom", "the whole stadium"). A question the video asks ("what happens if...") is answered by the chain, never by a lecture. Never write a beat that needs a photograph, a real person's face or a chart: this style has toy people and simple sets only.

picture.opening: Shot 1 is already in motion at frame 0: a figure mid-action in the set the first sentence names, the camera already pushing in. Never a title or an empty set.
picture.turn: A hard cut to a new shot on the first word of a turn or a re-opening, with a jolt or an impact burst at that moment.
picture.payoff: The shot with the answer, at the biggest scale of the video or on the strongest hit, held a little longer than the others.
picture.ending: Hold on the payoff picture to the last frame. No closing card, logo, recap or sign-off after it.

best_for: what happens if you do X: a chain of consequences that grows bigger with every step
an everyday situation pushed to an absurd scale (a room, then a stadium, then the planet)
a thought experiment or a scale comparison told as one person's story
a process or an event acted out by people moving through places
a physics or biology chain that ends in a cutaway or a cross-section
avoid_for: a real, named person, brand or product that must look like itself
abstract or text-heavy topics, numbers worked out, or a diagram of a mechanism (System Flow shows a mechanism)
a calm, atmospheric or sombre story where the place matters more than the action (Cartoon 3D fits it)
routing.cannot_show: photographs, or a real, named person or product as it really looks: everything is a toy figure and prop built from basic 3D shapes, so a real place is staged as a small invented set
signals: the script addresses the viewer as you and follows what happens next
each sentence names a new place or a bigger scale
the topic is a what-if or a why-doesn't-it-just question
a crowd, a planet or a cross-section is the payoff
the tone is playful, comic or energetic
